A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Orion hypersonic-flow surrogate study. The text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, and retained material can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original CFD simulations, neural-field and GNN experiments, ablations, inference timings and aerodynamic prediction errors, including Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds baseline comparisons, generalization experiments and extrapolation results in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The coordinate-and-AoA neural field, Fourier mappings and exponential no-slip/isothermal boundary enforcement are unchanged. v1 Equations 1–4 correspond to v2 Equations 4–7. Expanded explanations and additional comparator architectures do not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the fixed Orion geometry, steady Mach-5 flow-prediction task and existing 0°–45° CFD cases. The additional generalization studies repartition these angles and mesh points; they do not establish additional datasets, geometries or simulated flow regimes. The revised stated altitude is assessed under E3.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's GCN and GAT comparisons, v2 Tables 2–3 evaluate GIN, ChebNet, SGC, Graph U-Net, MeshGraphNet, GraphGPS, linear regression, ridge regression, nearest-neighbor regression and random forests. Section 7.3 also reports a GATv2 comparison with boundary conditions. GINO is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 retains the original training/validation configuration and adds high- and low-AoA extrapolation, sparse interpolation, and 80/20 and 50/50 spatial holdout protocols in Section 7.4. GraphGPS uses a 5,000-node subsampled graph. The stated CFD altitude changes from 50 km to 50 kft, without establishing that simulations were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 extends connectivity and Fourier-feature ablations to additional baselines and adds tests of extrapolation, sparse angular supervision and reduced spatial supervision. Appendix B.2 adds error analyses and flow-field case studies at 0°, 5°, 40° and 45°. The original boundary-condition, shock and wake analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 already reports means and standard deviations over three seeds in Tables 3–4. v2 retains this practice and extends mean/std reporting to additional results. No increased run count, new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–4 entries and the 15°/30° prediction errors remain unchanged. New results include GATv2 with boundary conditions at MSE 0.00274 ± 0.00009, Table 5 extrapolation/sparse-interpolation MSEs of 0.00621, 0.00720 and 0.00554, and Table 6 spatial-holdout MSEs of 0.00270 and 0.00487. Appendix B.2 adds component errors reaching 20.59%. These are additional results under their stated settings, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: New Section 3 explicitly formulates the compressible conservation equations, viscous stress, gas closure and temperature-dependent transport relations. This adds mathematical specification of the CFD background; the neural-field mathematics and Appendix A.2 wall-distance definition remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly frames the contribution as an application-focused empirical study and dataset contribution. The abstract specifies a fixed capsule geometry, and the introduction clarifies that physical enforcement concerns boundary conditions without conservation laws or PDE residuals. The central accuracy, Fourier-feature and computational-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1 Section 3.3's explicit warnings about invalid laminar and perfect-gas assumptions with a proof-of-concept justification, conditional gas-model qualifications and a stronger statement about straightforward extension to RANS. It also qualifies neural-operator limitations, refines the GNN smoothing explanation, and newly interprets extrapolation difficulty, wake orientation and stagnation-region errors in Section 7.4 and Appendix B.2.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies gas/transport constants, explains AoA-dependent mesh adaptation, documents GraphGPS's 5,000-node graph and reports approximately 50 minutes of training per node. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementation. Existing optimizer, architecture, hardware and wall-distance details remain; no new code or dataset access instructions appear.

R1.justification: v2 adds CFD-background and graph-architecture references and a focused discussion of GINO, acknowledging that geometry-aware operators address irregular discretizations. It more explicitly positions the work as an application study. The existing related-work narrative and relationship to the earlier 2D neural-field work remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The original narrative and section order largely remain. v2 makes localized prose edits, replaces simulator terminology with surrogate/inference terminology, adds explanatory preliminaries and mesh-adaptation subsections, and divides Appendix B into interpolation and extrapolation subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adds mesh and graph visualizations in Figures 4–5, four multi-panel extrapolation figures in Appendix B.2, and Tables 5–6. Tables 2–3 expand substantially. Earlier figures are retained with renumbering and relocation, alongside a publication header and associated layout changes.

improvement.justification: The broader comparator suite and targeted extrapolation, sparse-supervision and spatial-holdout tests substantially address v1's narrow empirical support for comparative performance and generalization. Clearer contribution scope and implementation documentation also help. Weaker physical-fidelity caveats and Appendix B.2's claim that errors are within 20%, despite a reported 20.59%, are drawbacks, but the substantially stronger validation provides a clear net improvement.
